messages.subject: Strange compilation error while using constraints
parts:
Hi,
I am working on a model that involves some constraints for certain parameters. Under some constraints, the model compilation fails consistently, while under similar constraints using the same parameters it compiles without any problems. To me it seems that it is not a problem with the model itself.

The relevant part of the model is the following:
....
    for (h_ in 1:nTargets) {
        dirParams[h_, 1:nSources] <- q[hierMatch[h_], 1:nSources] *
            sourceDirichPrior[1:nSources]
        alpha_[h_, 1:nSources] ~ ddirch(dirParams[h_, 1:nSources])
    }
    for (i_ in 1:nSources) {
        for (g_ in 1:nHierLevels) {
            q[g_, i_] ~ dlnorm(muQ, sdQ)
        }
    }
...

If I put the following constraint, nimble (v 0.12.1) fails (see error message below) to compile using compileNimble(model).
:

prior1_MO1 ~ dconstraint((alpha_[11, 1] + alpha_[12, 1] +
        alpha_[13, 1] + alpha_[14, 1])/4 > (alpha_[11, 2] + alpha_[12, 2] + alpha_[13, 2] + alpha_[14, 2])/4)

However, using the following two single constraints does work, although the same parameters are included:

prior1_MO1 ~ dconstraint((alpha_[11, 2] + alpha_[12, 2] + alpha_[13, 2] + alpha_[14, 2])/4 > 0.1)
prior2_MO1 ~ dconstraint((alpha_[11, 1] + alpha_[12, 1] + alpha_[13, 1] + alpha_[14, 1])/4 > 0.1)

Also, the the following does work, which has the same structure but other parameters as the failing constraint:
prior1_MO1 ~ dconstraint((alpha_[1, 1] + alpha_[2, 1] + alpha_[3, 1] + alpha_[4, 1] + alpha_[5, 1] + alpha_[6, 1] + alpha_[7, 1] + alpha_[8, 1] + alpha_[9, 1] + alpha_[10, 1])/10 > (alpha_[1, 2] + alpha_[2, 2] + alpha_[3, 2] + alpha_[4, 2] + alpha_[5, 2] + alpha_[6, 2] + alpha_[7, 2] + alpha_[8, 2] + alpha_[9, 2] + alpha_[10, 2])/10)

I was not able to identify the reason why the first one fails and the other ones not. Could this be a bug in Nimble or am I missing something? I can provide further info if neccessary.

Best Regards

messages.subject: Re: Strange compilation error while using constraints
parts:
Hi Marcus,

I believe the problem here is a glitch in how we create internal variable names. When dconstraint is used, we create an internal variable whose name is based on the syntax of the constraint. When the name gets too long we truncate the name, but in certain circumstances with names that are somewhat long but not very long, that process was not working correctly. This should be fixed in nimble version 0.12.2, which we just released on CRAN and are about to announce. (We haven't announced it yet because the MacOS binary package for nimble 0.12.2 for the ARM processor is not yet up on CRAN, so if your'e using a new M1-based Mac, you may have to wait another day or so to update.)

Let us know if updating doesn't fix the issue.

-chris

parts:
Hi Marcus, and thanks for your help off-list with a reproducible example.

It turns out that the issue you're having is very similar to an issue we fixed in version 0.12.2 but is distinct, so not solved by updating to 0.12.2. Basically, what happens is that we introduce new variables in some cases (e.g., to represent the condition within dconstraint). We name the new variable based on the syntax in the model and in some cases such as yours, the name can get to be very long, in which case we truncate it. That usually works fine, except in your case, you triggered a situation where the length of the name was long but not too long, such that the truncation was happening in one part of our processing but not another part, causing inconsistent naming. 

I've fixed this on our devel branch on GitHub, so you can install from there. It will be fixed in the next release but that will probably not occur for a few months.

-chris

On Tue, Mar 1, 2022 at 10:41 AM Chris Paciorek <christophe...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Marcus,

I believe the problem here is a glitch in how we create internal variable names. When dconstraint is used, we create an internal variable whose name is based on the syntax of the constraint. When the name gets too long we truncate the name, but in certain circumstances with names that are somewhat long but not very long, that process was not working correctly. This should be fixed in nimble version 0.12.2, which we just released on CRAN and are about to announce. (We haven't announced it yet because the MacOS binary package for nimble 0.12.2 for the ARM processor is not yet up on CRAN, so if your'e using a new M1-based Mac, you may have to wait another day or so to update.)

Let us know if updating doesn't fix the issue.

-chris

christophe...@gmail.com schrieb am Donnerstag, 10. März 2022 um 23:39:02 UTC+1:
Hi Marcus, and thanks for your help off-list with a reproducible example.

It turns out that the issue you're having is very similar to an issue we fixed in version 0.12.2 but is distinct, so not solved by updating to 0.12.2. Basically, what happens is that we introduce new variables in some cases (e.g., to represent the condition within dconstraint). We name the new variable based on the syntax in the model and in some cases such as yours, the name can get to be very long, in which case we truncate it. That usually works fine, except in your case, you triggered a situation where the length of the name was long but not too long, such that the truncation was happening in one part of our processing but not another part, causing inconsistent naming. 

I've fixed this on our devel branch on GitHub, so you can install from there. It will be fixed in the next release but that will probably not occur for a few months.

-chris

On Tue, Mar 1, 2022 at 10:41 AM Chris Paciorek <christophe...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Marcus,

I believe the problem here is a glitch in how we create internal variable names. When dconstraint is used, we create an internal variable whose name is based on the syntax of the constraint. When the name gets too long we truncate the name, but in certain circumstances with names that are somewhat long but not very long, that process was not working correctly. This should be fixed in nimble version 0.12.2, which we just released on CRAN and are about to announce. (We haven't announced it yet because the MacOS binary package for nimble 0.12.2 for the ARM processor is not yet up on CRAN, so if your'e using a new M1-based Mac, you may have to wait another day or so to update.)

Let us know if updating doesn't fix the issue.

-chris
